pointsOfInterest.shortDescription: Located on the Gangtok-Lachung Highway, seven different waterfalls harmonize and cascade down rugged cliffs. Features a footbridge and cafeteria. Best viewed during monsoon.
Headquarters of North Sikkim offering an incredible vantage point for the Kanchenjunga range. Panoramic mountain views on clear days.
The geographical heart of North Sikkim where Lachen and Lachung rivers meet to form the Teesta River. Located near Chungthang, surrounded by high mountain walls.
Also known as Amitabh Bachchan Falls due to its impressive height. One of the tallest and most powerful waterfalls in the region with a vertical drop.
One of the highest lakes in the world at 17,800 feet. Sacred to Buddhists, Sikhs, and Hindus. A portion remains unfrozen even in extreme winter—considered miraculous.
A quiet alpine valley for acclimatization before Gurudongmar. Known for wooden houses, nomadic lifestyle, and landscapes that shift from green to snow-covered.
Located above Thangu, famous for alpine meadows and proximity to the Tibetan border. Offers views of meandering rivers and snow-clad peaks.
A serene religious site built in 1858 with traditional Tibetan architecture and colorful murals. Offers a panoramic view of Lachen village.
The 'Valley of Flowers' — a sprawling meadow surrounded by Himalayas. Home to Shingba Rhododendron Sanctuary with 24+ rhododendron species and hot springs.
The last civilian outpost before the international border at 15,300 feet. Snow is almost always present, a favorite for winter experiences.
An off-beat destination near Lachung with spectacular snow-capped peak views. Popular for snow sports and frozen waterfalls. Requires army permits.
Perched on a slope across the river, one of the most culturally significant sites. Hosts famous Mask Dance during festivals, surrounded by apple orchards.
